4928.t: From Phoenician (compare Hebrew נֵרְדְּ (nērd), Aramaic נִרְדָּא (nirdā), Akkadian 𒆠𒆗 (HIRIM /⁠lardu⁠/), Arabic رَنْد (rand), Old South Arabian 𐩧𐩬𐩵 (rnd)), possibly from Sanskrit नलद (nálada, “Indian narde”) (although a Semitic-to-Indian loan has also been…

4930.t: Derived from νομίζω (nomízō, “to use customarily”) + -μα (-ma, “nominal suffix”).

4923.t: From νέμω (némō, “to pasture; to graze”) + -ός (-ós, deverbal nominal suffix). Compare ἀγρός (agrós).

4920.t: Sometimes derived from a Proto-Indo-European *me(-)mbʰ-e-, and compared with obsolete English mump (“to cheat, swindle”), Gothic 𐌱𐌹𐌼𐌰𐌼𐍀𐌾𐌰𐌽 (bimampjan, “to mock”).

4968.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *per- Proto-Indo-European *-is Proto-Indo-European *-h₂ Proto-Indo-European *-ih₂ Proto-Indo-European *périh₂ Proto-Hellenic *péřřa Ancient Greek πεῖρα (peîră) Proto-Indo-European *-h₂ Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂…

4907.t: From μετα- (meta-, indicating change) + φέρω (phérō, “bear, carry”).

4985.t: Deverbative or denominative formation on the basis of a form *pēd-, which appears to be a lengthened grade of Proto-Indo-European *ped- (“to walk, step”).

4931.t: Of unclear origin. Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *new- (“to make a push, nod”).

4986.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kʷo- (“interrogative, relative stem”) and maybe *h₂el- (“to grow”). Cognate with Latin quālis.

4926.t: From νωθής (nōthḗs, “sluggish, slothful”) + -ρός (-rós, adjective suffix). The origin of νωθής (nōthḗs, “slow, indolent, stubborn”) is disputed.

4916.t: Unclear. The word has been linked with μυών (muṓn, “cluster of muscles”) because both marrow and muscles are soft in texture.

4909.t: From μετα- (metă-, “behind”) + φρήν (phrḗn, “midriff”), literally “the part behind the midriff”.

4939.t: οἶκος (oîkos, “home”) + -ίζω (-ízō, “a suffix forming a verb from a noun”)

4956.t: From παραλογίζομαι (părălogĭ́zomai, “to cheat; to use fallacies”) + -μός (-mós).

4936.t: From οἰκέω (oikéō, “inhabit, dwell”) + -τός (-tós, “A suffix creating verbal adjectives of possibility, either active or passive”)
